0.body: Bazel rules for parsing Kconfig files and generating equivalent Bazel build settings. A kconfig repository exposes each config symbol as a Bazel build setting flag (bool_flag, int_flag, or string_flag) whose default matches the Kconfig-declared default. It also generates a config.h header (via rules_cc_autoconf ) that reflects the active flag values, so C/C++ code can consume the configuration with #include "config.h".
0.title: rules_kconfig

1.body:
Add the dependency to your MODULE.bazel: bazel_dep(name = "rules_kconfig", version = "{version}") Then register a kconfig repository via the module extension: kconfig = use_extension("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:extensions.bzl", "kconfig")
kconfig.repo( name = "my_kconfig", kconfig = "//:Kconfig",
)
use_repo(kconfig, "my_kconfig") The tree is parsed by the Linux kernel's own Kconfig parser, which the extension downloads for the host (see Parser ). menuconfig is the kernel's own mconf too, built from the same sources with bison, flex and ncurses from the registry, launched by a small C++ program built from source.

12.body:
You can supply a .config file to override Kconfig defaults. Pass the defaults attribute when declaring the repository: kconfig.repo( name = "my_kconfig", kconfig = "//:Kconfig", defaults = "//:.config",
) A symbol whose definition runs $(shell,...) would take a value from the host that generates the repository. Where a .config can set the symbol (it has a prompt whose condition holds) the repository rule does not bake the host's value in: without a defaults file the flag's default is the falsey one of its type, and with one the symbol must be set there, or the rule fails with an error listing the symbols to add. Where no .config can set the symbol, as it has no prompt or its dependencies are off (the kernel's CC_IS_GCC and the compiler probes behind it), it takes the value the Kconfig tools calculate, the one rendered.config shows; settings_labels replaces such a symbol with a build-time value.
12.title: Providing defaults via .config

13.body:
A Kconfig tree may read variables with $(NAME) or option env, and its $(shell,...) commands run in an environment. Give the variables the tree expects with env, per repository, so that several configurations of one tree can come out of a workspace: kconfig.repo( name = "my_kconfig_arm64", kconfig = "@my_tree//:Kconfig", defaults = "//configs:arm64_defconfig", env = { "ARCH": "arm64", "SRCARCH": "arm64", },
) A variable env does not name is read from the repository rule's own environment (--repo_env). The variables are recorded in the manifest and apply to kconfig.overrides layered on the repository, and the generated repository's kconfig_library carries them, with the version, for menuconfig. The upstream example generates repositories this way and checks them against the trees' own conf.
13.title: The tree's environment variables

14.body:
A tree's $(shell,...) macros may run a compiler or linker named by a variable while the tree is parsed, and what they answer decides which symbols are visible and selected. A repository rule runs before any toolchain is resolved, so it cannot ask Bazel for the compiler of a platform; it can run a binary of a toolchain repository that is already downloaded. env_labels maps such a file to a variable, and its path is the value: kconfig.repo( name = "my_kconfig_arm64", kconfig = "@my_tree//:Kconfig", env = {"ARCH": "arm64", "SRCARCH": "arm64"}, env_labels = { "@llvm_toolchain_llvm//:bin/clang": "CC", "@llvm_toolchain_llvm//:bin/ld.lld": "LD", },
) The binary runs on the host, as a cross compiler does; the paths go into the manifest for kconfig.overrides.

14.title: Tools from a toolchain's repository

15.body:
The menuconfig rule runs mconf, the make menuconfig terminal UI of the kernel's scripts/kconfig, built from the parser version that serves the release the tree is written for, so that what it accepts and writes is what the repository rule reads. Add a target to your BUILD.bazel: load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:menuconfig.bzl", "menuconfig") menuconfig( name = "menuconfig", config = ".config", kconfig = "@my_kconfig//:lib",
) Then run it: bazel run //:menuconfig The TUI reads and writes the file config names, relative to the root module's workspace. The file must exist there: the launcher resolves the path on disk and refuses one that leads outside the workspace or to no file, so menuconfig edits a file of your own and nothing else. Everything else comes from the kconfig_library: the files, the release (kconfig_version) and the variables the tree reads (env, env_labels), which the lib of a generated repository carries as its kconfig.repo was given them. mconf runs over the library's files in the runfiles: the root's directory there is $(srctree) and the working directory, as the repository rule runs a tree's $(shell,...) commands. A tree whose Kconfig files run its own scripts lists them in the library's srcs. Everything is found through the runfiles and BUILD_WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY; no path is absolute or resolved through symlinks. A repository generated with defaults, and a kconfig.overrides over a config, have a menuconfig of their own over that file when it is the root module's: bazel run @my_kconfig//:menuconfig. The next build after a save is under the new configuration, as the repository reads the file. mconf is a curses program over POSIX, so menuconfig is for Linux and macOS. On Windows the target is incompatible: bazel build //... skips it, and bazel run reports why.

2.body:
Kconfig has no version of its own: the language is whatever the kernel's scripts/kconfig accepts at a release, and that has changed over the years. kconfig_version names the kernel release a tree is written for, and the tree is then parsed and resolved exactly as that release's conf would: For a kernel tree, its release: 6.12, or 6.12.7. For a project with its own copy of the parser, the release the copy was synced from. A tree that uses ---help---, optional choices or option needs a version before 6.10, where the kernel dropped them. Any major.minor or major.minor.patch is accepted; the default is 6.17, the newest release checked. rules_kconfig carries the parser of the releases where the language changed, and a version is served by the newest one at or below it: kconfig_version parser 6.12 and newer Linux 6.12 4.19 to 6.11 Linux 4.19 A version below 4.19 is an error. The version is recorded in the generated repository's manifest, and the kconfig.overrides layered on the repository use the same parser; they take no version of their own. kconfig.repo( name = "my_kconfig", kconfig = "@my_tree//:Kconfig", kconfig_version = "4.19",
)
2.title: Kconfig versions

24.body: load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:defs.bzl", "kconfig_library") kconfig_library(name, deps, srcs, env, env_labels, kconfig_version, root) Collect Kconfig source files into a single provider for use by menuconfig and repository rules. All source files must be real (non-generated) files. If a single source is provided, it is automatically treated as the root. When multiple sources are present, set root explicitly to indicate the top-level Kconfig entry point. Transitive sources from deps are included in the provider, as are their variables; the library's own take precedence. The release the tree is written for (kconfig_version) and the variables its files read (env, env_labels) are properties of the tree, so they live here, and menuconfig takes them from the provider. The lib of a generated repository carries what its kconfig.repo was given. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required deps Other kconfig_library targets whose sources should be included transitively. List of labels optional [] srcs Kconfig source files, and any script their $(shell,...) commands run, so that menuconfig has them. Must be real (non-generated) files. List of labels optional [] env Environment variables the Kconfig files read ($(NAME), option env), by name. Dictionary: String -> String optional {} env_labels Files whose path is a variable's value (a compiler the tree's $(shell,...) runs), each label mapped to the variable's name. Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} kconfig_version The kernel release the tree is written for, as kconfig.repo takes it (6.12, 4.19); the newest checked when empty. String optional "" root The top-level Kconfig file. Inferred automatically when srcs contains exactly one file. Label optional None

26.body: load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:defs.bzl", "menuconfig") menuconfig(name, config, kconfig) Edit a .config interactively with mconf, the make menuconfig terminal UI. mconf is built from the kernel's scripts/kconfig of the parser version that serves the release the tree is written for (kconfig_version of its kconfig_library), the code the kconfig repository rule reads the tree with, so what the TUI accepts and writes is what the build reads. The tree's variables (env, env_labels of the library) are set for it by a small C++ launcher built from source, with the toolchain mconf needs anyway. mconf is a curses program over POSIX, so the target is for Linux and macOS: on Windows it is incompatible, which //... skips and bazel run reports. Run with bazel run. The TUI reads and writes the file config names, relative to the root module's workspace, which must exist there: the launcher resolves the path on disk, and refuses one that leads outside the workspace or to no file. A repository generated from a defaults file, or kconfig.overrides over a config, has a menuconfig of its own over that file when the file is the root module's. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required config Workspace-relative path of the .config file to read and write; an existing file of the root module's workspace. String required kconfig The kconfig_library of the tree: its files, release and variables. Label required

27.body: load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:defs.bzl", "KConfigInfo") KConfigInfo(env, env_files, kconfig_version, root, srcs) A Kconfig source tree: its root file, every source file (direct and transitive), the release it is written for and the variables it reads. FIELDS Name Description env dict[str, str]: The environment variables the tree's Kconfig files read ($(NAME), option env), by name. env_files dict[str, File]: Variables whose value is a file's path (a compiler the tree's $(shell,...) runs), by name. kconfig_version str: The kernel release the tree is written for (kconfig_version of kconfig_library); empty for the default. root Optional[File]: The top-level Kconfig file that the parser reads. May be None when a library contributes sources but is not itself a root. srcs depset[File]: All Kconfig source files (direct and transitive) reachable from this library.

29.body:
load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:defs.bzl", "kconfig_overrides_repository") kconfig_overrides_repository(name, config, kconfig, tools, wasm_module) Overlay .config values onto an existing kconfig repository. Reads the manifest from the source kconfig repository to locate the Kconfig tree, then reparses it where the source repository read it, with the parser of the kconfig_version the manifest records, as kconfig_repository did, with a user-provided .config file. If the source repository was itself created with a .config, the overrides are stacked on top of those base values. The tree's $(shell,...) commands answer as they did for the source repository, from its manifest, and rendered.config is written as the source repository's was (write_invisible). Generates a defs.bzl containing a Starlark transition and wrapper rule that apply the overrides. Values explicitly set on the command line take precedence over the overlay. The generated defs.bzl creates the transition and rule: rule description kconfig_override_transition A transition that applies transitions for each default in .config with_kconfig_overrides A rule similar to alias that applies kconfig_override_transition to the target Use with_kconfig_overrides to wrap a kconfig-dependent target: load("@base_kconfig_override//:defs.bzl", "with_kconfig_overrides") with_kconfig_overrides( name = "config", actual = ":consumer_of_base",
) ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this repository. Name required config .config file with override values. Label required kconfig Label to the kconfig manifest from the source kconfig repository (e.g. @my_kconfig//:my_kconfig). Label required tools The native builds of the parser (kconfig_tool), used where the WebAssembly module cannot be, each mapped to the <os>-<cpu> of the host that runs it (linux-x86_64), or to host for a build of this host, taken over the platform's. Only the host's is fetched. The kconfig module extension provides the release's builds, and as host the one RULES_KCONFIG_TOOL names. Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} wasm_module The WebAssembly build of the parser (kconfig.wasm), used on Bazel 9.3 or newer with --experimental_repository_ctx_execute_wasm, unless RULES_KCONFIG_USE_WASM=0 (through --repo_env) asks for the native build. The kconfig module extension provides the release's module, or the one RULES_KCONFIG_WASM names. Label optional None
29.title: kconfig_overrides_repository

3.body: The parser is the Linux kernel's scripts/kconfig, of every release in Kconfig versions , with this repository's generators, in one program that a release of rules_kconfig ships in two builds. The kconfig extension declares a repository for each, kconfig_parser_wasm and kconfig_parser_tool_<os>_<cpu>, the same set on every host, and a generated repository downloads only the one it runs, through Bazel's repository cache, the first time. Both builds generate the same repository, byte for byte. bazel fetch --all and bazel vendor --all fetch every build, so an output base, repository cache or vendor directory filled on one host serves another offline.
3.title: Parser

30.body: load("@rules_kconfig//kconfig:defs.bzl", "kconfig_repository") kconfig_repository(name, apparent_name, defaults, env, env_labels, kconfig, kconfig_version, settings_labels, settings_options, tools, wasm_module, write_invisible) Parse a Kconfig file tree and generate a Bazel repository with build settings. The generated repository contains a bool_flag, int_flag, or string_flag for every config symbol found in the Kconfig tree, plus a cc_library target (:config) providing a config.h header that reflects the active flag values. The Kconfig source tree is symlinked into kconfig_srcs/ and a kconfig.manifest.json records the root file and all visited files. A repo-named symlink (e.g. @my_kconfig//:my_kconfig) points to the manifest for downstream consumers. The Kconfig tree is parsed by the kernel's parser of the release kconfig_version names, as the WebAssembly module a release of rules_kconfig carries (Bazel 9.3 or newer with --experimental_repository_ctx_execute_wasm) or as the release's native build for the host; both generate the same repository. Prefer using the kconfig module extension rather than calling this rule directly. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this repository. Name required apparent_name The user-facing repository name (used for the repo-named symlink). Defaults to the canonical name. String optional "" defaults Optional .config file with explicit symbol values that override Kconfig defaults. Label optional None env Environment variables for the Kconfig tree: what $(NAME) and option env read, and the environment of $(shell,...) commands, over the repository rule's own environment (--repo_env). The kernel's tree reads ARCH, SRCARCH, CC, LD and others its Makefile exports, so that several architectures' repositories can be generated in one workspace. The variables are recorded in the manifest and apply to kconfig_overrides_repository layered on the repository. Dictionary: String -> String optional {} env_labels Files as environment variables for the Kconfig tree: each label's path is the value of the variable it maps to, over env. For the tools a tree's $(shell,...) probes run, CC, LD or RUSTC, a label into a downloaded toolchain's repository (@llvm_toolchain_llvm//:bin/clang) runs that toolchain's binary on the host; a repository rule cannot resolve the toolchain Bazel would pick for a platform. Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} kconfig The root Kconfig file to parse. All files referenced via source directives are followed automatically. Label required kconfig_version The kernel release the tree is written for: 6.17 (the default), 6.12.7, 4.19. Kconfig has no version of its own, so this is the release of the kernel tree, or the one a project's copy of scripts/kconfig was synced from. The tree is parsed and resolved as that release's conf would, by the newest parser rules_kconfig builds at or below the version (6.12, 4.19); a version below the oldest is an error. The version is recorded in the manifest, and the overrides layered on the repository use the same. String optional "6.17" settings_labels Map of CONFIG_* names to label strings for user-provided rules that replace generated flags. The label must point to a target that provides BuildSettingInfo. Use this for symbols whose values depend on the build configuration (e.g. toolchain-derived values like compiler version). Dictionary: String -> String optional {} settings_options Optional map of CONFIG_* names to lists of string values for generated config_settings. Dictionary: String -> List of strings optional {} tools The native builds of the parser (kconfig_tool), used where the WebAssembly module cannot be, each mapped to the <os>-<cpu> of the host that runs it (linux-x86_64), or to host for a build of this host, taken over the platform's. Only the host's is fetched. The kconfig module extension provides the release's builds, and as host the one RULES_KCONFIG_TOOL names. Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} wasm_module The WebAssembly build of the parser (kconfig.wasm), used on Bazel 9.3 or newer with --experimental_repository_ctx_execute_wasm, unless RULES_KCONFIG_USE_WASM=0 (through --repo_env) asks for the native build. The kconfig module extension provides the release's module, or the one RULES_KCONFIG_WASM names. Label optional None write_invisible Write the symbols the configuration makes invisible too, to rendered.config as # CONFIG_X is not set or with the type's empty value, each in its place, and to config.h as that value, for sources that expect a CONFIG_X for every symbol, as BusyBox's do; the kernel's tools leave them out. Boolean optional False

Use this for symbols whose values depend on the build configuration (e.g. toolchain-derived values like compiler version). Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} settings_options Optional map of CONFIG_* names to lists of string values for generated config_settings. Dictionary: String -> List of strings optional {} write_invisible Write the symbols the configuration makes invisible (no prompt applies and no default does) too: to rendered.config, each in its place, as # CONFIG_X is not set or with the type's empty value (CONFIG_X="", CONFIG_X=0), and to config.h as that value, so that a string or int is defined, an empty one. The kernel's tools leave such a symbol out of .config and autoconf.h, so that #ifdef can tell; for sources that expect a CONFIG_X for every symbol, as BusyBox's conf writes it. Boolean optional False
33.title: repo

4.body: On Bazel 9.3 or newer with common --experimental_repository_ctx_execute_wasm in .bazelrc, the repository rules run the parser as a WebAssembly module with repository_ctx.execute_wasm. The module cannot touch the filesystem, the environment or a shell, so the rules do it on its behalf: they read the source tree ahead, every directory's listing and every Kconfig* file, and hand it to the module, which asks for what that leaves, $(shell,...) commands, files with other names and the variables a Kconfig names, in a further round. Everything read is recorded as an input of the repository, environment variables through repository_ctx.getenv, so a repository that ran no host command is reproducible and Bazel may take it from the repo contents cache instead of generating it again. With Bazel 10, --experimental_repository_ctx_wasm_compilation compiles the module to JVM bytecode, which is several times faster than interpreting it.
4.title: WebAssembly

5.body: Where Bazel cannot run the module, Bazel 7 and 8 or without the flag, the rules run the same program built natively for the host, with repository_ctx.execute under the same protocol. A release has native builds for Linux and Windows on x86_64 and aarch64 and for macOS on aarch64. --repo_env=RULES_KCONFIG_USE_WASM=0 takes the native build where Bazel could run the module: interpreted, the module is many times slower than the native build, which on a large tree is minutes against a second.
5.title: Native

6.body: A source checkout of rules_kconfig carries no builds. Name one with RULES_KCONFIG_WASM or RULES_KCONFIG_TOOL through --repo_env: an absolute path or a URL, for instance the outputs of bazel build --config=wasm32 @rules_kconfig//kconfig/private/parser:kconfig_wasm and bazel build @rules_kconfig//kconfig/private/parser:kconfig_tool. RULES_KCONFIG_WASM_INTEGRITY and RULES_KCONFIG_TOOL_INTEGRITY may give the integrity (sha256-...) of a URL.
6.title: A source checkout

7.body: For a Kconfig file such as: config FOO bool "Enable FOO" default n config COUNT int "Count" default 3 The generated repository @my_kconfig contains: Target Description @my_kconfig//:CONFIG_FOO bool_flag (default False) @my_kconfig//:CONFIG_COUNT int_flag (default 3) @my_kconfig//:config cc_library providing config.h @my_kconfig//settings.CONFIG_FOO_Y config_setting matching CONFIG_FOO = true @my_kconfig//settings.CONFIG_FOO_N config_setting matching CONFIG_FOO = false @my_kconfig//settings.CONFIG_COUNT_3 config_setting matching CONFIG_COUNT = 3
7.title: Generated repository
